portion_doctrine: Segments 91-100 are a video transcript (NOT about Astro) featuring a comprehensive Cursor AI tutorial. Content focuses on Cursor 2.0 agent features, building landing pages, creating meme generators with image upload/template support, debugging UI issues, and running multiple agents concurrently. Primary value: hands-on patterns for AI-assisted full-stack development using Cursor's agent model, real-time browser inspection, and iterative debugging workflows. Title mismatch: document labeled 'astro claude websites 3x faster' but actually covers Cursor 2.0 code editor (no Astro framework content detected).
operating_rules: Always create an empty folder first; projects live in folders (called directories in code)
Files must have extensions (.py, .md, .txt, .html, .js) to label file type
Frontend = visible components (UI users see/click); Backend = invisible code (data, features)
Running locally = executing code on your computer, not renting a server
Use Chat mode for asking questions, Composer mode for big multi-file features
Inline editing (Ctrl+K) for small targeted code changes within a file
Image-to-code capability: pass an image (Figma, screenshot, photo) and Cursor generates HTML/CSS matching the design
Git repository required for running multiple agents concurrently; git = checkpointing/saving code snapshots
Each new chat isolates agent work; prevents chaos from continuous multi-agent prompting
Browser inspection feature (@browser) shows agent live screenshot; high context-window cost
Accept/reject diffs from agent suggestions before applying to project
named_methods: Composer mode (multi-file generation for big features)
Chat window with code search (Ctrl+L or Cmd+L; search context with Ctrl+Enter)
Inline editing (highlight code + Ctrl+K for targeted changes)
Agent feature: tool-enabled research (web search, doc reading, multi-page discovery)
Multi-agent concurrent execution (requires Cursor Max plan)
Browser inspection via @browser flag (captures live screenshot for context)
Image-to-code translation (design screenshot or photo to working HTML/CSS)
Terminal execution (local dev server, npm/python commands)
specific_numbers: 3 main UI parts: left (file tree), middle (editor), right (AI panel)
3 agent models mentioned: Composer 1, Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT (in multi-agent test)
~5 seconds to generate simple game code
Meme app test: multi-agent solving (3 agents running concurrently, Composer 1 finishes fastest)
specific_tactics: Start with clear vision + sketches before prompting (AI performs best with specific discrete tasks, not vague requests)
Use @file or @folder to add context before asking questions
Link documentation (PDFs, web docs) in chat context to guide AI generation
Ask agent to explain code segments before modifying them
For UI bugs, ask agent to look at browser and describe the problem, then propose fix
Use multiple agents on complex bugs, then apply the best solution
Create new chat for each major feature to prevent agent confusion
Undo + re-apply diffs if first agent attempt fails; don't continue prompting same chat thread
Highlight broken code section + ask agent specifically what went wrong
prompts: Do some research on the company [name] and create me a landing page. Run this landing page locally when you are done.
Create a new HTML file that contains this form, make it look exactly like this [image].
I added a folder named assets and it has some photos that I would like to use as templates for memes. I would also like to still have the ability to upload my own image.
When I add the second text to a meme, it overwrites the first text. Please make sure this does not happen. I want to be able to have different text on the image.
Look at the browser. The text rendered in a single line causing overflow. I want to be able to split lines.
How do I play the game?
Where are my recipes defined? [for code search]
I want to set up git for this project.

IDE navigation (Cursor vs VS Code ecosystem)

Multi-agent concurrency shows agents 'thinking' in parallel; Composer 1 consistently finishes before Claude/GPT (speed vs quality trade-off hint)
@browser screenshot captures mid-interaction state, allowing agent to see overflow bugs humans must describe in words
